slides.title: Family WhatsApp group *fight?*
slides.sub: Chachu just left the family group. A prayer from the Rigveda, one of the world's oldest books, shows a better way.

slides.title: How it *blew up*
slides.body: Someone forwarded a message. Chachu replied in CAPITALS. Mummy took sides. By night, Chachu had left the group. Sound familiar?

slides.deva: आ नो भद्राः क्रतवो यन्तु विश्वतोऽदब्धासो अपरीतास उद्भिदः ।
slides.iast: ā no bhadrāḥ kratavo yantu viśvato 'dabdhāso aparītāsa udbhidaḥ
slides.meaning: Let good thoughts come to us from every side, with nothing stopping them, breaking through. (First half of the verse.)
slides.ref: Rigveda 1.89.1, Rishi Gotama Rahugana, to all the gods

slides.title: Word by word: *4 key words*
slides.body: Bhadrāḥ = good, kind. Kratavaḥ = thoughts, ideas. Yantu = let them come. Viśvataḥ = from every side.

slides.title: Who said it, and *to whom*
slides.body: The text says: Rishi Gotama sang this to all the gods together. It opens a hymn asking for a long, good and safe life.

slides.title: Every side means *every side*
slides.body: For us today: a good idea can come from anyone, even the chachu you disagree with. Keep the door open. You don't have to win.

slides.title: Before you post in the *family group*
slides.body: Screenshot this. Ask: Is it true? Is it kind? Does it help anyone here? If not, don't send it. Call Chachu instead.

slides.title: Send this to your *family group admin*
slides.sub: Save it for the next family WhatsApp group fight, and share it with the one who keeps the peace. Follow @sutraverselife for real-life lessons from ancient wisdom.
